app.subtitle: Network Atlas
app.fictional: Fictional example environment: {org}, all sites, people and IP addresses are invented.

header.technicalHint: Full detail for IT: VLANs, addresses, commands

map.title: Network map
map.simple: See all four sites and how they are connected. Tap a site to look inside.
map.technical: HQ and three clinics in a hub-and-spoke IPsec VPN. One VLAN plan for every site: 10.<site>.<vlan>.0/24.

simulator.title: Failure simulator
simulator.simple: Switch something off and see who can no longer work, and what to do first.
simulator.technical: Inject power, link and service faults. The engine returns the chain reaction, test order and fix, and it knows about redundancy.

issues.title: Common issues
issues.simple: The everyday problems in a clinic and how they get solved.
issues.technical: Ticket catalogue: symptom, likely causes by probability, checks in order, solution.

opening.title: New clinic opening
opening.simple: How the München clinic gets its IT, from signed lease to opening day.
opening.technical: Opening playbook: site survey, ISP order, procurement, pre-staging at HQ, installation, validation, go-live, hypercare.

standards.title: Standardization and automation
standards.simple: Every clinic gets the same kit. That makes openings fast and support easy.
standards.technical: Standard hardware, one site template with variables, staged firmware rollout, Ansible, macOS zero-touch.

haLab.title: HA lab
haLab.simple: How the central servers keep running when one of them fails.
haLab.technical: vSphere cluster with 3 hosts: HA restart, admission control with N+1, vMotion, DRS, anti-affinity.

privacy.title: Data protection (GDPR)
privacy.simple: Where personal data lives and how it is protected.
privacy.technical: Data flows and measures per location: clinic, transit, HQ, cloud, organization.

monitoring.title: Monitoring and on-call
monitoring.simple: How problems are noticed early, before the clinic has to call.
monitoring.technical: Status board, on-call example with runbook, early warnings, release flow with software engineering.

about.title: About this project
about.what: The IT of a veterinary clinic chain, planned end to end: network, clinic openings, troubleshooting, standards, high availability, data protection and monitoring.
about.fictional: {org} does not exist. Sites, people, hostnames and IP addresses are invented, and dashboards are simulations. Lead times, prices and retention periods are illustrative placeholders.
about.how: A static web app without backend, login or external requests. All content comes from validated data files in English, German and Turkish.

try.switch: Switch off a clinic switch and follow the chain reaction.
try.host: Let a server host fail and watch HA restart its VMs.
try.opening: Tick off the München playbook until the clinic goes live on the map.
